title: Route each JTBD step to its layer(s) and canonical call sequence

facts.note: Primary trigger: task text declares, assigns or reviews a JTBD step, whether or not any routing has been declared yet.
Discovery hint only, not a scope restriction: these are the usual places JTBD steps are declared; the rule applies to a JTBD step declaration in any artifact.
Discovery hint only, not a prerequisite: the rule applies whenever a JTBD step is declared, assigned or reviewed, regardless of phase; a phase observer would only help prioritise.
No detector exists (implementation.type none); a reviewer/LLM checks every declared JTBD step for layers and sequence against the canonical table.

fires: A JTBD step (e.g. resolve) is declared or assigned in any artifact and no primary layer or call sequence is stated for it yet.
A planner doc lists JTBD steps but omits a step's primary layer or gives a sequence that differs from the canonical one.
A reviewer checks a plan, wagon or WMBT containing JTBD steps to confirm each step is placed in the layered architecture.
doesNotFire: Coder implementing code inside one layer with no JTBD step being declared, assigned or reviewed.
Text that uses words like 'monitor' or 'define' in ordinary prose, not as a JTBD step.
Choosing or renaming the step taxonomy itself (governed by planner.steps.jtbd-taxonomy).

given: A JTBD step (define, locate, prepare, confirm, execute, monitor, modify, resolve, conclude) appears in work being planned, in any artifact, with or without existing routing
when: the step is declared, assigned or reviewed
then: Declare for every JTBD step its primary architecture layer(s) and its canonical ordered call sequence of layer.operation tokens across presentation, application, domain and integration, exactly as in the canonical step table.
prefer: execute [domain, application]: presentation.command → application.use_case → domain.mutate → integration.persist
monitor [presentation]: presentation.query → application.query → integration.read → application.aggregate → presentation.display
resolve [application]: application.event → application.use_case → domain.policy → integration.call_external → integration.persist
conclude [integration, application]: application.use_case → domain.validate → integration.persist → integration.archive
Write sequences as ordered layer.operation tokens so steps are mechanically routable.
avoid: Leaving any step without primary layer(s) or call sequence.
Reordering, dropping or inventing tokens versus the step's canonical sequence.
Layer names outside presentation, application, domain, integration.
Adding extra steps to the taxonomy to fit a sequence instead of routing via the table.
why: Binding steps to layers and call sequences keeps the JTBD taxonomy minimal yet routable, so a step can be mechanically placed into the layered architecture.
evidence: Every JTBD step declared in any artifact lists its primary layer(s) matching layers_by_step.
Every declared call sequence matches sequence_by_step for that step token-for-token and in order.

Worked check: define → layers [domain], sequence [presentation.command, application.use_case, domain.create, integration.persist]; monitor → layers [presentation], sequence [presentation.query, application.query, integration.read, application.aggregate, presentation.display].
verifier_detail: Term layers_by_step: the primary architecture layer(s) each step lands in. define=[domain]; locate=[application]; prepare=[application]; confirm=[application]; execute=[domain, application]; monitor=[presentation]; modify=[application]; resolve=[application]; conclude=[integration, application]. In prefer[0..8] the bracketed list after the step name is this value.

Term sequence_by_step: the canonical ordered call sequence across layers for each step, written as layer.operation tokens. Comparison is ordered and exact per token (see prefer[0..8] for the full table).

Source examples: resolve routes application.event → application.use_case → domain.policy → integration.call_external → integration.persist; conclude routes application.use_case → domain.validate → integration.persist → integration.archive.
No mechanical detector: implementation.type none; compliance is reviewer/LLM judged. A step missing routing entirely is a finding, not out of scope.
